documents.title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed eCollection eComments Requested; Extension Without Change, of a Previously Approved Collection; Procurement Collusion Strike Force Complaint Form
documents.summary: The Department of Justice Antitrust Division is requesting approval from the Office of Management and Budget to extend an information collection for the Procurement Collusion Strike Force Complaint Form, which allows the public to report potential antitrust crimes affecting government procurement. The document invites public comments for 30 days until November 5, 2026.
programs: Procurement Collusion Strike Force Complaint Form

documents.title: Public Hearing
documents.summary: This document announces a public hearing by the National Commission on the Future of the Navy scheduled for October 8, 2026, to discuss actions necessary to secure America's future maritime seapower with Navy, Marine Corps, and Joint uniformed leaders. The hearing is established in accordance with the National Defense Authorization Act of 2023 and is open to the public.
agencies: National Commission on the Future of the Navy
programs: National Commission on the Future of the Navy
statutes: Fiscal Year 2023 National Defense Authorization Act

documents.title: Precision Navigation Systems: Challenges Remain with Fielding New Capabilities
documents.summary: This GAO report examines the Department of Defense's efforts to modernize GPS and develop complementary positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) systems to address ongoing delays and security threats. The report finds that while some progress has been made on modernized GPS military code (M-code) receivers and complementary PNT systems, challenges remain with fielding and integration across fragmented military service efforts.

documents.title: PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.; Notice of Institution of Section 206 Proceeding and Refund Effective Date
documents.summary: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission issued a notice on September 29, 2026, instituting a Section 206 proceeding to investigate whether PJM Interconnection's proposed changes to establish the Reliability Backstop Procurement are unjust, unreasonable, or unlawful. The refund effective date for the proceeding is the date of publication of this notice in the Federal Register.

documents.title: Mortgage Lending: Newly Enacted Restrictions May Help Curb Unwanted Solicitations While Preserving Comparison Shopping
documents.summary: This GAO report examines mortgage trigger lead marketing, where credit reporting agencies sell homebuyers' information to lenders and brokers for solicitations. The document analyzes benefits and drawbacks of this practice and how the 2025 Homebuyers Privacy Protection Act's restrictions may affect homebuyers.

documents.title: Quantum Computing: Federal Actions Needed to Prepare for Emerging Cyber Threat
documents.summary: This Government Accountability Office (GAO) report examines the threat that quantum computers pose to federal agency cryptography and evaluates the extent to which 24 federal agencies have prepared to transition to post-quantum cryptography. The report finds that none of the 24 selected agencies fully addressed preparatory practices needed to mitigate the threat of cryptographically relevant quantum computers.
agencies: Office of the National Cyber Director

documents.title: General Services Administration Acquisition Regulation; GSAR Implementation of Executive Order 14275, Acquisition of Utility Services
documents.summary: GSA proposes to amend the General Services Administration Acquisition Regulation (GSAR) part 541 to implement Executive Order 14275 by relocating utility services acquisition procedures from FAR part 41 to GSAR to streamline the federal procurement process. The proposed rule aligns GSA guidance with FAR Council requirements and directs agencies to use GSA's areawide contracts and subject-matter expertise for utility acquisitions.

documents.title: Proposal of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Regarding Transactions Involving the A7 Network's Sub-Agents
documents.summary: FinCEN is proposing a rule that would prohibit financial institutions from processing certain fund transfers involving the A7 Network, a money laundering service with ties to Russia and Iran, which FinCEN has determined to be a primary money laundering concern related to Russian illicit finance. The proposed rule is issued under authority granted by the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act and the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022.
statutes: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022

documents.title: Public Health Preparedness: Action Needed to Address National and Biosecurity Risks Associated with Disposal of Federal Laboratory Equipment
documents.summary: This GAO audit report examines the sale of laboratory equipment by the Department of Health and Human Services and U.S. Department of Agriculture, finding that 9 pieces of equipment on the Commerce Control List were sold without proper reporting and that the agencies have not adequately assessed biosecurity risks associated with equipment disposal. The report recommends that HHS revise its policy and GSA create a standard approach for reporting controlled items to mitigate national security risks.
agencies: Department of Health and Human Services

documents.title: Internet of Things: OMB Action Needed to Ensure Agencies Secure Their Networked Devices
documents.summary: This GAO report examines federal agencies' implementation of Internet of Things (IoT) and networked device security requirements issued by the Office of Management and Budget. As of September 2026, most of the 22 civilian CFO Act agencies reviewed had not fully complied with OMB's requirements to establish and maintain inventories of networked devices, with only seven agencies having addressed all three requirements.

documents.title: Fraud in Federal Programs: Limited Beneficial Ownership Information Available on Awardees
documents.summary: This GAO report examines fraud in federal programs involving hidden beneficial ownership of companies receiving federal awards such as contracts, grants, and Medicare payments. The report finds that limited beneficial ownership information is available across federal and state data sources, leaving hundreds of billions of dollars in federal awards vulnerable to fraud, and notes that implementation of statutory requirements for a federal contractor beneficial ownership database has been delayed.
statutes: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021

documents.title: Director of National Intelligence: Status of Open GAO Recommendations
documents.summary: This document is a GAO report on the status of recommendations made to the Director of National Intelligence from July 2011 through September 15, 2026. As of September 15, 2026, the Office of the DNI has implemented 76 of 139 recommendations (55 percent), with 57 recommendations remaining open that could improve intelligence management and oversight if fully implemented.
agencies: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
statutes: James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023

documents.title: Small Business Research Programs: Better Data Could Improve Insight into Companies’ Success
documents.summary: This GAO report examines the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) programs, which issued $4.4 billion in awards from 11 federal agencies in fiscal year 2024. The report finds that incomplete data on commercialization outcomes prevents agencies from effectively evaluating the success of open and conventional topic awards, as small businesses submitted required reports for less than half of their prior awards.
statutes: SBIR and STTR Extension Act of 2022

documents.title: Coast Guard: Additional Action Needed to Address Marine Firefighting Challenges
documents.summary: This Government Accountability Office (GAO) report examines nearshore marine fires and the challenges the U.S. Coast Guard faces in coordinating firefighting responses, finding that 886 fires occurred between 2015 and 2025 with about one quarter resulting in deaths, injuries, significant damage, or vessel loss. The report identifies gaps in the Coast Guard's efforts including the need for consistent field personnel coordination, hands-on firefighter training, information sharing mechanisms, guidance on vessel response plan activation, and expanded authority to require response plans for vessels using alternative fuels.
statutes: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026

documents.title: Cybersecurity Regulations: Industry Panelists Identify Duplication and Conflicts and Ways to Address Them
documents.summary: This GAO report documents findings from a July 16, 2026 panel discussion with industry representatives from energy, financial services, and healthcare sectors who identified duplication and conflicts among federal cybersecurity regulations. Industry participants recommended harmonizing regulations through consistent reporting timeframes and thresholds, and establishing a lead agency to coordinate incident reports.
agencies: Office of the National Cyber Director

documents.title: IT Systems Annual Assessment: DOD Should Improve IT Fraud Risk Management Practices
documents.summary: This Government Accountability Office (GAO) report assesses the Department of Defense's management of 18 major IT business programs, examining their progress on cost, schedule, and performance metrics from fiscal years 2024 through 2026. The report finds that while DOD is making efforts to improve IT investment management, several programs lack adequate fraud risk awareness training, software development tracking, and cybersecurity planning to meet departmental deadlines.
agencies: DOD Office of the Chief Information Officer
statutes: National Defense Authorization Act for FY 2019
